items.title: How a small per-run failure chance still shows up reliably in CI
items.description: A test that fails only 5% of the time per run still looks 'basically fine' on any single run — but CI runs a suite hundreds of times a week. This uses the standard probability of at least one failure across N independent runs (1 minus the chance of passing every single time) to show why even a small flake rate becomes visible fast once a suite runs often enough.

params.name: perRunFailPercent
params.label: Chance this test fails on any one run

items.compute: const p = params.perRunFailPercent / 100; const probAtLeastOne = Math.round((1 - Math.pow(1 - p, params.numRuns)) * 1000) / 10; return { probAtLeastOne };

outputs.label: Chance of seeing at least one failure
